ConnectionStrings._comment: Overridden by environment variables in Docker (see compose.yaml). These localhost defaults are for a standalone `dotnet run` against a local Postgres + Redis.

Jwt._comment: Fallback issuer/audience used only when a resolved tenant carries none of its own.

Resend._comment: Outbound email for verification codes. Supply the real ApiKey via the Resend__ApiKey environment variable / your secrets store — never commit it.

MyPassKeys._comment_DeploymentHosts: Hostnames where THIS MyPassKeys installation is reachable (e.g. 'auth.example.com', 'localhost:5205'). Requests on any other host must match a per-tenant Tenant.Hosts entry or are 404'd. Tenants cannot claim a deployment host.
MyPassKeys._comment_IssuerBaseUrl: Base for auto-deriving each tenant's immutable JwtIssuer as '{IssuerBaseUrl}/t/{tenantId}'. MUST be an exact string match with the resource server's issuer base. Overridden to http://localhost:5205 in appsettings.Development.json.
MyPassKeys._comment_Bootstrap: On a fresh deployment a management tenant is seeded with these origins/issuer/audience and the user from Tenant:BootstrapOwnerEmail is granted the tenantadmin role in it (re-applied on every startup so the operator can always log back in). After the initial seed these origin/issuer/audience values are NOT re-applied — edit the tenant via PUT /tenants/{id} instead.
MyPassKeys._comment_KeyEncryptionKey: REQUIRED base64 32-byte key that encrypts tenant signing keys at rest. Supply via the MyPassKeys__KeyEncryptionKey environment variable in production (see compose.prod.yaml / .env.example). A dev-only value lives in appsettings.Development.json. The app refuses to start without one.

Tenant._comment: Email guaranteed to hold tenantadmin in the management tenant. Re-applied on every startup so the operator can always log back into the admin portal.

ForwardedHeaders._comment: Trust only these proxies to set X-Forwarded-*. Defaults to loopback when both lists are empty. Add your Docker bridge / reverse proxy CIDRs in production (e.g. '172.16.0.0/12', '10.0.0.0/8'). For Cloudflare-fronted setups, add Cloudflare's published IP ranges.
